statement: The geometric monodromy group in its action on the unique generic solution is the trivial group S1.

group.description: Trivial permutation group on one solution

source.location: Theorem8.1 and Table7, arXiv v1 printed page24

scope: The generic fibre for plane quartics of genus 3 through 14 points. For real-count assertions, all prescribed points and lines (including any specified contact point) are real and satisfy the genericity assumptions.

origin.inheritance_basis: A reduced generic complex fibre of cardinality one has trivial permutation action; for generic real inputs conjugation fixes its unique solution.

notes:
Elementary deduction from the recorded complex count one. Complex conjugation preserves the fibre for real input data, so its unique point is fixed and the solution curve is defined over R. A permutation action on a singleton is trivial. These deductions are supplied here explicitly; they are not attributed as separate theorems in the cited paper. The assertion concerns real solution curves, not reality of every point on a real curve.

Zeuthen 1873 predicted these quartic characteristic numbers; Vakil completes their rigorous verification. Vakil supplies the inspected proof; Zeuthen’s prediction remains historical attribution in these notes. Singleton real/monodromy conclusions are deductions from the count.

H. G. Zeuthen, Almindelige Egenskaber ved Systemer af plane Kurver (1873, article ID zeuthen_1873_plane_curve_systems). Historical attribution recorded by the cited supporting article. No separately inspected result locator in this earlier article was recorded for this result.
